title: Grid frequency control
summary: The synchronous grid's frequency as the measure of its power balance, the control loops that hold it, and the trading schedule whose steps show up in it.

concepts.label: Grid frequency
concepts.description: The rotation rate shared by every synchronous generator in Continental Europe, nominally 50 Hz.

facts.text: Energy-Charts publishes the frequency measured every second in Freiburg.

children.label: Frequency deviation
children.description: Frequency minus 50 Hz in mHz: positive means more power fed in than used.

children.label: Rate of change of frequency
children.description: df/dt in mHz/s (RoCoF): how fast the imbalance moves the frequency, set by the imbalance over the grid's inertia.

children.label: Deterministic frequency deviation
children.description: The regular jump after each quarter-hour and hour, from stepwise generation schedules.

concepts.label: Frequency control
concepts.description: The cascade of controllers that holds the frequency near 50 Hz.

children.label: Frequency containment reserve
children.description: Primary control: a proportional (droop) response within seconds, 3000 MW across Continental Europe at ±200 mHz.

children.label: Automatic frequency restoration reserve
children.description: Secondary control: an integral controller per control area that brings the frequency back to 50 Hz within minutes.

children.label: Grid inertia
children.description: The kinetic energy of rotating machines; it limits RoCoF after a sudden imbalance and shrinks as inverter-based generation grows.

concepts.label: Electricity market time unit
concepts.description: The block in which power is traded and scheduled: 15 minutes in the European day-ahead market since October 2025.

children.label: Generation schedule
children.description: Planned output per block; steps at block boundaries while demand changes smoothly.
